question: A 28-year-old woman with a history of migraines presents to your office due to sudden loss of vision in her left eye and difficulty speaking. Two weeks ago she experienced muscle aches, fever, and cough. Her muscle aches are improving but she continues to have a cough. She also feels as though she has been more tired than usual. She had a similar episode of vision loss 2 years ago and had an MRI at that time. She has a family history of migraines and takes propranolol daily. On swinging light test there is decreased constriction of the left pupil relative to the right pupil. You repeat the MRI and note enhancing lesions in the left optic nerve. Which of the following is used to prevent progression of this condition?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "28-year-old woman with sudden vision loss" -> "history of migraines" -> "MRI shows enhancing lesions in left optic nerve" -> "suggestive of optic neuritis" -> "possible multiple sclerosis" -> "treatment needed to prevent progression" -> "Natalizumab is used for multiple sclerosis" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Patient presents with vision loss and speech difficulty" -> "previous episode of vision loss" -> "MRI reveals enhancing lesions" -> "indicates inflammatory demyelination" -> "condition likely related to multiple sclerosis" -> "Natalizumab is a disease-modifying therapy" -> "prevents progression of multiple sclerosis" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Sudden loss of vision in left eye" -> "decreased pupil constriction on swinging light test" -> "MRI shows lesions in optic nerve" -> "consistent with optic neuritis" -> "potential diagnosis of multiple sclerosis" -> "treatment options include disease-modifying therapies" -> "Natalizumab is effective in preventing progression" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Patient has muscle aches, fever, and cough" -> "symptoms improving but persistent cough" -> "previous similar episode of vision loss" -> "MRI shows enhancing lesions" -> "indicative of optic neuritis" -> "risk of multiple sclerosis" -> "Natalizumab indicated for prevention" -> 75%
analysis: The patient's symptoms and MRI findings suggest a diagnosis of multiple sclerosis (MS), particularly given the history of vision loss and the presence of enhancing lesions in the optic nerve. Natalizumab is a disease-modifying therapy used to prevent progression in patients with relapsing forms of MS. The other options listed (dexamethasone, methotrexate, infliximab, adalimumab) are not first-line treatments for MS. Therefore, the most appropriate choice for preventing progression of this condition is natalizumab.
